You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Treasury Buyback Size to At Least Double; Anthropic May File IPO by Month-End; Bitcoin Approaching Golden Cross Signal (August 21, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
Chair Walsh to Deliver First Jackson Hole Speech Since Taking Office
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Walsh will speak at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium on August 28, addressing inflation targets, productivity, demographics, and global economic shocks.
With inflation remaining above the 2% target for five consecutive years, markets are watching whether he will provide more concrete anti-inflation language beyond “we are dealing with it.”
The current federal funds rate target range is 3.5%–3.75%. Market Impact : The speech is viewed as a key window into the new chair’s communication style and policy priorities, and may influence subsequent rate-path pricing.
International Commodities
Trump’s Hard Line on Iran Continues; Oil Prices Supported
President Trump continues to signal economic pressure on Iran, with Brent crude rising toward the $93 area.
Geopolitical uncertainty and supply concerns remain the dominant near-term drivers of oil prices. Market Impact : Elevated oil prices reinforce sticky-inflation concerns and weigh on rate-sensitive assets.
Macroeconomic Policy
Treasury Buyback Size to At Least Double; Bessent Teases New Fiscal Consolidation Measures
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that long-term Treasury buybacks will be “at least doubled,” with single operations next month potentially exceeding the previously planned $4 billion, and signaled new fiscal consolidation measures as early as this weekend or early next week.
President Trump has tasked him and the budget director with advancing the work; the toolkit includes cracking down on fraud, cutting certain state-level spending, and higher tariff revenues. Market Impact : Buybacks temporarily suppressed yields, but markets remain skeptical of their durability. Long-end yields rebounded on Thursday, prompting U.S. equities to give back gains.
II. Market Review
Commodities Forex Performance
Spot Gold : Approx. $4,511/oz, -0.19%
Spot Silver : Approx. $68/oz, -0.11%
WTI Crude : Approx. $86/bbl, -0.59%
Brent Crude : Approx. $88.8/bbl, -0.52%
US Dollar Index (DXY) : Approx. 98.8, -0.05%
Driver Analysis : Expanded Treasury buybacks briefly pushed long-end yields lower, but the effect faded quickly. Combined with higher oil prices driven by geopolitical factors, inflation concerns re-emerged. Gold oscillated between rising yields and safe-haven demand, while silver showed relative resilience. Institutional views hold that near-term commodities are dominated by “buyback fade + higher oil,” creating a linkage of rising oil → inflation expectations → higher yields → pressure on risk assets.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approx. $73,600, +5.88%
ETH : Approx. $2,338, +3.04%
Crypto Total Market Cap : $2.55 trillion, +3.8%
Market Liquidations : Total liquidations $957 million, of which short liquidations $785 million
Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map : Current BTC price around $73,659. Residual long-liquidation leverage remains notable in the $70,000–$73,000 zone below; a break of key support could trigger successive liquidations. Short-liquidation pressure is accumulating in the $74,000–$76,000 area above; further upside could spark short covering and amplify gains. Short-term leverage focus has clearly shifted upward, with the multi-short battleground concentrated near $73,000–$74,000.
Spot ETF Net Flows : Yesterday’s net inflow $517 million; current 24-hour dynamic net inflow $103 million.
Driver Analysis : Residual momentum from Trump’s push for crypto legislation and the White House meeting, combined with earlier short squeezes, has kept BTC and ETH firm. Rising yields have exerted some pressure on risk assets, yet the crypto market has remained relatively independent of the U.S. equity pullback. Institutional consensus points to short-term drivers rooted in policy narrative and liquidity; attention remains on subsequent fund flows and leverage dynamics.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at 52,759.21, -1.32%
SP 500 : Closed at 7,641.16, -0.87%
Nasdaq : Closed at 26,067.17, -1.00%, with tech and consumer under pressure
Tech Giants Dynamics

Performance Summary Driver Analysis : The Mag 7 mostly closed lower. Apple and Amazon led the declines, while Nvidia was relatively resilient. The fading effect of Treasury buybacks, the rebound in long-end yields, and higher oil prices jointly suppressed risk appetite. AI hardware and consumer tech came under simultaneous pressure, with capital shifting toward more defensive positioning.
Sector Movers Observation
Biotech / Pharmaceuticals – Sharp Pullback
Representative stocks : Moderna -approx. 23.55%; Nasdaq Biotechnology Index -approx. 2.92%.
Drivers : Profit-taking and volatility realization after the previous session’s surge.
Crypto-Related Stocks – Continued Strength

Event Overview : Broadcom is reportedly in discussions with Blackstone, Apollo and others on approximately $100 billion in debt financing to support chip and infrastructure purchases by Anthropic and other AI firms. Market Interpretation : Analysts believe the deal would help Broadcom expand its AI-chip market share and intensify competition with Nvidia. The large financing also underscores that AI infrastructure capital expenditure remains elevated. Investment Implications : Watch the progress of the financing and its actual impact on company orders.

Market Interpretation : Rising yields and declining risk appetite left even consumer-electronics leaders unable to decouple. Investment Implications : The medium-term thesis still rests on new products and services; near-term moves will track the overall market.

Market Interpretation : Crypto-asset prices and the regulatory narrative remain the primary drivers; volatility is significantly higher than that of traditional tech stocks. Investment Implications : High-beta exposure requiring close tracking of Bitcoin price action and legislative progress.
